Simulate stratified-random survey

Source: R/sim_survey.R
sim_survey.Rd

Simulates a stratified-random survey on a population produced by sim_distribution(). Supports optional catchability functions, sampling caps, and custom set locations.

sim_survey(
  sim,
  n_sims = 1,
  q = sim_logistic(),
  trawl_dim = c(1.5, 0.02),
  resample_cells = FALSE,
  binom_error = TRUE,
  min_sets = 2,
  set_den = 2/1000,
  lengths_cap = 500,
  ages_cap = 10,
  age_sampling = "stratified",
  age_length_group = 1,
  age_space_group = "division",
  custom_sets = NULL,
  light = TRUE,
  q_by = "age",
  maturity_sampling = "aged"
)

Arguments

sim

A simulation object returned by sim_distribution(). Omit to create a sim_survey_spec configuration for sim_surveys(), without running a simulation or consuming random numbers.

n_sims

Number of surveys to simulate. Supply common replicate counts on sim_surveys() rather than inside a configuration. With existing batch metadata, an omitted count (or NULL) inherits its replicate identifiers; an explicit count must agree with them. Be cautious: large values may consume significant memory. Use sim_survey_parallel() if many simulations are needed.

q

A closure (e.g., sim_logistic()) for simulating catchability. Returned values must range between 0 and 1.

trawl_dim

Trawl width and distance (same units as the grid).

resample_cells

Logical. If TRUE, allows grid cells to be resampled. May introduce bias, as depletion is applied at the cell level.

binom_error

Logical. Should binomial error be imposed? If FALSE, stratified estimates at older ages may be biased due to rounding zeros.

min_sets

Minimum number of sets per stratum.

set_den

Set density (sets per grid unit squared). Warning: May error if set_den is high and resample_cells = FALSE, because allocated sets may exceed available cells.

lengths_cap

Maximum number of lengths measured per set.

ages_cap

Cap on the number of ages to sample, depending on age_sampling type:

  • If "stratified": maximum per length bin (via age_length_group) and per age_space_group (e.g., "division", "strat").

  • If "random": maximum number of fish aged per set.

age_sampling

Type of age sampling strategy: "stratified" (default) or "random".

age_length_group

Width of length bins for stratified age sampling. Ignored if age_sampling = "random".

age_space_group

Spatial scale for stratified age sampling. Options: "division" (default), "strat", or "set". Ignored if age_sampling = "random".

custom_sets

A data.table of set locations (same structure as returned by sim_sets()). If NULL, set locations are generated automatically.

light

Logical. If TRUE, drops some objects from output to reduce memory footprint.

q_by

Basis of catchability: "age" (the historical default) or "length". Length-based catchability is evaluated on the growth model's discrete length-group labels. Availability integrates catchability over the length-age key; caught lengths follow that selected distribution.

maturity_sampling

Fish examined for maturity: "aged" (default), "measured", or "none". Binary states follow the population maturity model. Unexamined mature values are missing and maturity_observed is FALSE. With light = FALSE, sample_truth retains latent states for measured fish. All length/age sampling finishes before maturity is drawn for every measured fish, independently of this observation mask. Switching only this argument preserves existing samples, catches, and overlapping maturity states. An older object lacking a maturity model can retain number-only sampling with "none".

Value

A list including:

  • Rounded simulation results

  • Set location details

  • Sampling results

Includes:

  • N: true population

  • I: individuals available to the survey

  • n: individuals caught by the survey

When sim is omitted, returns a sim_survey_spec list of settings. samp$weight gives deterministic kilograms for every simulated caught fish; unmeasured fish weights are latent truth, not extra measurements. setdet$kg and samp_totals$kg_caught sum all caught fish, not just measured lengths. With light = FALSE, full_setdet$kg gives catch weight by set and age. Legacy objects without a weight model retain missing weights and positive-catch totals, with zero kilograms for zero catches. No defaults are silently assigned.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- sim_abundance(ages = 1:5, years = 1:5) |>
  sim_distribution(grid = make_grid(res = c(20, 20))) |>
  sim_survey(n_sims = 5, q = sim_logistic(k = 2, x50 = 3))

plot_survey(sim, which_year = 3, which_sim = 1)


# }
